CLINICAL RELEVANCE: This review supports the integration of deprescribing practices into geriatric psychiatric care but underscores the need for individualized decision-making. Clinicians should use PIM lists and deprescribing tools as aids, while prioritizing patient-centered discussions about risks and benefits.

articles.title: French psychiatric caregivers' perceptions of psychedelics: A national survey.
articles.authors: Buot A, Burdairon JD, Mallet L, et al.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: The use of psychedelic substances such as LSD, psilocybin, and dimethyltryptamine is currently being re-evaluated for their therapeutic potential in psychiatry. While international clinical research had started in the 2010s, France only initiated its first psychedelic trials in 2024. This study aimed to explore the knowledge, perceptions, and attitudes of French mental health professionals regarding the use of psychedelics in clinical and recreational settings. MATERIALS AND METHODS: An anonymous online survey was conducted between December 2023 and January 2024 among psychiatry caregivers in France. The questionnaire included 19 items across five sections: demographic information, knowledge of psychedelics, perception of their therapeutic and recreational use, and personal experimentation with psychoactive substances. Data was analyzed using linear and ordinal regressions, controlling for age, gender, profession and experience with ketamine. RESULTS: A total of 298 respondents participated, primarily from public hospitals. Most were psychiatrists (41.4%) or psychologists (20.4%). About 88% had heard of medical studies on psychedelics, with high awareness of psilocybin and ketamine use in treatment-resistant depression. However, awareness of other therapeutic indications was limited. Fifty-three percent rated the therapeutic benefit-risk ratio of psychedelics as favorable, whereas 61% rated recreational use as dangerous. Favorable perception of therapeutic use was
articles.summary:
BACKGROUND: With France only recently initiating psychedelic trials in 2024, this national online survey examined French psychiatric caregivers’ knowledge, attitudes, and perceptions toward therapeutic and recreational use of psychedelics (LSD, psilocybin, DMT) among 298 respondents (December 2023–January 2024).

FINDINGS: 88% had heard of medical studies, with high awareness of psilocybin and ketamine for treatment-resistant depression. 53% rated the therapeutic benefit-risk ratio as favorable, while 61% viewed recreational use as dangerous. Favorable therapeutic views correlated with male gender, personal psychedelic experience, and ketamine practice; in a subgroup (psychiatrists, residents, nurses), only ketamine practice remained significant. Personal experimentation predicted more positive attitudes toward recreational use.

INTERPRETATION: The study suggests moderate, cautious openness to therapeutic psychedelics among French caregivers, shaped by personal and clinical exposure—especially ketamine. The cross-sectional survey design, modest sample (n=298), and reliance on self-report limit causal inference and generalizability beyond public hospital staff. Findings reflect attitudes at a single time point, before France’s 2024 trials, so future shifts are likely.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Current attitudes do not yet justify changes in routine practice, but the strong influence of ketamine exposure implies that early trial participation and education may shape future acceptance among French psychiatric teams.

articles.title: Steroidomic Differences Among Clozapine, Olanzapine, and Risperidone in Male Patients with First-Episode Psychosis, Including a Treatment-Resistant Schizophrenia Subgroup.
articles.authors: Valeš K, Holubová K, Španiel F, et al.
articles.abstract: Clozapine (Clo) is the most effective antipsychotic for treatment-resistant schizophrenia (TRS), yet the mechanisms underlying its unique clinical profile remain insufficiently understood. Neuroactive steroids (NASs) influence neuronal excitability, neuroplasticity, inflammation, and stress responses-domains disrupted in schizophrenia-and may contribute to antipsychotic pharmacodynamics. This pilot study examined whether Clo exhibits a distinctive steroidomic pattern compared with olanzapine (Ola) and risperidone (Ris) in male patients with first-episode psychosis, including a clinically defined TRS subgroup receiving Clo. Serum collected after group-specific treatment durations (Clo: 17.7 ± 12.4; Ola: 13.9 ± 1.9; Ris: 12.9 ± 1.3 months) was analyzed by GC-MS/MS, with steroidogenic enzyme activities inferred from precursor-product molar ratios as proxies of metabolic balance. Statistical evaluation included age-adjusted ANCOVA, OPLS, multiple regression, and trend-based analysis of coordinated pathway-level shifts. Although Ola increased several steroid concentrations, its overall and unconjugated trends did not differ significantly from Clo (p = 0.515 and p = 0.409). At the multivariate level, however, the two profiles were significantly discriminated (OPLS: R2Y = 50.8%, CV-ANOVA p = 0.011), indicating that the difference lies in the coordinated pattern rather than the global magnitude of change. Clo showed a distinctive exploratory pattern: lower DHEA, higher 5α-reduced pre
articles.summary:
BACKGROUND: This pilot cross-sectional study investigated whether clozapine (Clo) produces a distinctive neuroactive steroid (NAS) profile compared with olanzapine (Ola) and risperidone (Ris) in male patients with first-episode psychosis, including a treatment-resistant schizophrenia (TRS) subgroup receiving Clo. The goal was to explore mechanistic differences that might underlie clozapine’s unique clinical efficacy.

FINDINGS: After 12–18 months of treatment, serum steroidomic profiles were analyzed by GC-MS/MS. Global steroid concentrations did not differ significantly between Clo and Ola (p = 0.515), but multivariate orthogonal partial least squares (OPLS) analysis distinguished Clo from Ola with R²Y = 50.8% and CV-ANOVA p = 0.011. Clo showed lower DHEA, higher 5α-reduced pregnane NAS, altered androgen turnover, reduced CYP17A1 lyase proxy activity, and a mild increase in the cortisol-to-cortisone ratio. Clo was also clearly distinguished from Ris by broad steroid increases. Sample size and follow-up duration were not explicitly stated.

INTERPRETATION: The study’s internal validity is limited by its small, male-only, cross-sectional design and lack of independence among steroid pathways, which increases the risk of spurious associations. While the multivariate separation between Clo and Ola is statistically robust, the clinical meaning remains exploratory. The absence of longitudinal data and adjustment for multiple comparisons further constrains causal inference. The observed steroidomic pattern may reflect neuroprotective or GABAergic modulation, but this is speculative without functional validation.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: These preliminary findings do not yet justify changes in antipsychotic selection. They suggest a potential biomarker signal that warrants larger, longitudinal, sex-balanced studies with functional assays to determine whether steroidomic profiles can predict or mediate treatment response.

articles.title: Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists and Incident Cardiovascular Events and Death in Treated Serious Mental Illness, Type 2 Diabetes, and Obesity.
articles.authors: Governor SB, Dávila-García DM, Rivera-Segarra E, et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Adults with serious mental illness (SMI), type 2 diabetes, and obesity have elevated cardiovascular risk. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have established cardiometabolic benefits in the general population, but their effects in SMI are unclear. We evaluated whether GLP-1RA use was associated with lower risks of incident myocardial infarction (MI), heart failure (HF), and all-cause death. METHODS: This was a retrospective propensity score-matched cohort study of 218 043 adults with SMI, type 2 diabetes, obesity, and active antipsychotic or antidepressant medications in the TriNetX database (73 health care organizations). Outcomes were incident MI, HF, and all-cause death at 1 and 3 years. The primary exposure was GLP-1RA use versus nonuse; secondary analyses examined semaglutide or tirzepatide. Exploratory analyses evaluated sex, race, and sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitor and dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitor use. RESULTS: GLP-1RA use was associated with lower risks of incident MI, HF, and all-cause death. Risk differences at 1 and 3 years were -0.007 and -0.010 for MI, -0.011 and -0.018 for HF, and -0.039 and -0.065 for death (all P<0.001). Semaglutide or tirzepatide use was also associated with lower risks of MI, HF, and death (all P<0.001). Findings were directionally consistent after accounting for sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitor and dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitor use. CONCLUSIONS: Adults with treated SMI, type 2 diabetes,
articles.summary:
BACKGROUND: This retrospective propensity score–matched cohort study (n=218 043) in the TriNetX database examined whether glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) reduce incident myocardial infarction (MI), heart failure (HF), and all-cause death over 1 and 3 years in adults with serious mental illness (SMI), type 2 diabetes, and obesity who were receiving antipsychotic or antidepressant treatment.

FINDINGS: GLP-1RA use was associated with lower absolute risk differences at 1 and 3 years: MI −0.7 % and −1.0 %, HF −1.1 % and −1.8 %, and all-cause death −3.9 % and −6.5 % (all P<0.001). Semaglutide or tirzepatide showed similar reductions. Results remained directionally consistent after adjustment for SGLT2 inhibitors and DPP-4 inhibitors.

INTERPRETATION: The large, propensity-matched cohort suggests clinically meaningful reductions in cardiovascular events and mortality with GLP-1RA therapy in this high-risk population. However, residual confounding from unmeasured variables (e.g., lifestyle, adherence, severity of SMI) and reliance on administrative codes limit causal inference. The magnitude of benefit is plausible given known cardiometabolic effects of GLP-1RAs, but replication in prospective trials is needed.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: These findings support consideration of GLP-1RAs in patients with SMI, type 2 diabetes, and obesity on psychotropic medications, particularly when cardiometabolic risk is high. Clinicians should weigh benefits against adverse effects and cost while awaiting confirmatory evidence.

articles.title: Phenotypic Complexity and Diagnostic Utility of Exome Sequencing in ASD: Real-World Insights from Colombia.
articles.authors: Rodríguez Gutiérrez DA, Cárdenas Prieto R, Rueda-Gaitán P, et al.
articles.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a genetically heterogeneous condition; however, genomic data from Latin American populations remain limited. We investigated the molecular and phenotypic landscape of ASD in 916 Colombian patients who underwent whole-exome sequencing (WES) between 2022 and 2025. Clinical and genomic data were retrospectively analyzed, and phenotypes were standardized using Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO) terms. Variants were classified per ACMG/ClinGen guidelines, and we assessed phenotypic burden, predictors of molecular diagnosis, copy number variants (CNVs), and functional convergence of candidate genes. A molecular diagnosis was identified in 112 patients (12.2%), including 82 with variants in ASD-associated genes or regions and 30 with findings related to other clinical features. We identified 16 novel pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants, along with 10 CNVs. Among trio-based patients, 70.9% of molecular diagnoses were de novo. Higher phenotypic burden was associated with molecular diagnosis, and global developmental delay was the strongest predictor after correction for multiple testing. Functional enrichment analysis of candidate genes showed convergence on pathways related to neuronal development, synaptic function, and ion transport. These findings highlight the genetic and phenotypic heterogeneity of ASD and support the value of integrating standardized genomic and phenotypic characterization in Colombian populations.
articles.summary: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a genetically heterogeneous condition; however, genomic data from Latin American populations remain limited. We investigated the molecular and phenotypic landscape of ASD in 916 Colombian patients who underwent whole-exome sequencing (WES) between 2022 and 2025. Clinical and genomic data were retrospectively analyzed, and phenotypes were standardized using Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO) terms.

articles.title: Dose-dependent efficacy and safety of centanafadine in patients with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder: A systematic review of the latest evidence.
articles.authors: Gul D, Khan S, Baral K, et al.
articles.abstract: Centanafadine is a multimodal norepinephrine-dopamine-serotonin reuptake inhibitor (NDSRI) that has been evaluated for the treatment of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) across pediatric, adolescent, and adult populations. This systematic review aimed to evaluate the efficacy, safety, and tolerability of centanafadine compared with placebo, with particular emphasis on dose-response patterns across different age groups. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) were searched from database inception to July 2026. Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials evaluating centanafadine in patients with ADHD were eligible for inclusion. The Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) tool was used to assess the risk of bias. Because of differences in populations, formulations, dosing regimens, outcome measures, and reported effect estimates, findings were synthesized narratively rather than quantitatively. Four randomized trials reported in three publications, including 1845 randomized participants, were included. In children, high-dose centanafadine significantly improved attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder rating scale, version 5 (ADHD-RS-5) scores compared with placebo (-16.3 vs. -10.8; p < 0.001), whereas the low-dose group did not demonstrate a statistically significant difference (mean difference [MD] -2.7; 95% confidence interval [CI], -6.0 to 0.5; p = 0.10). In adolescents, 328.8 mg significantly improved A
articles.summary:
BACKGROUND: This systematic review assessed the efficacy and safety of centanafadine, a multimodal norepinephrine-dopamine-serotonin reuptake inhibitor (NDSRI), for ADHD across pediatric, adolescent, and adult populations using randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials. The review synthesized dose-response patterns and adverse events narratively due to heterogeneity in study designs.

FINDINGS: Four RCTs (1,845 participants) were included. In children, high-dose centanafadine significantly improved ADHD-RS-5 scores vs. placebo (-16.3 vs. -10.8; p < 0.001), while low-dose did not (MD -2.7; 95% CI -6.0 to 0.5; p = 0.10). In adolescents, 328.8 mg improved ADHD-RS-5 scores (MD -4.3; p = 0.0006; Cohen’s d = -0.40), but 164.4 mg did not (p = 0.3016). In adults, both 200 mg and 400 mg/day significantly improved AISRS scores (LSMDs -2.74 to -4.42; p ≤ 0.039). Treatment-emergent adverse events ranged from 25%–39% in children, 23.8%–50.3% in adolescents, and 17.6%–31.8% in adults, with higher rates at higher doses in some groups.

INTERPRETATION: The evidence suggests dose-dependent efficacy of centanafadine, particularly in children and adolescents, with smaller but significant effects in adults. However, the review highlights critical limitations: only four RCTs from three publications, short-term follow-up, no active comparators, and potential industry sponsorship bias. The effect sizes (e.g., Cohen’s d = -0.40 in adolescents) are modest and may not translate to clinically meaningful improvements for all patients. The safety profile appears dose-related, warranting caution in dosing.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Centanafadine may offer an additional treatment option for ADHD, but its place in therapy remains uncertain due to limited long-term data and lack of comparative trials. Clinicians should weigh modest efficacy against adverse effects and await further independent, head-to-head studies before considering it a first-line agent.

articles.title: Exercise-based interventions for postpartum depressive symptoms: a systematic review and network meta-analysis of exercise modality and weekly volume.
articles.authors: Liu S, Tan Y, Zang L
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To synthesize randomized evidence on exercise-based interventions for postpartum depressive symptom scores and to explore comparative signals across exercise types and pragmatic weekly-volume categories using pairwise and network meta-analysis. METHODS: Eight bibliographic databases were searched from inception and updated through July 23, 2026, with three trial registries searched in the final update, for randomized controlled trials of postpartum exercise interventions reporting Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS) scores. Pairwise meta-analysis used mean differences (MDs), and network meta-analyses evaluated exercise-type and weekly-volume nodes. The review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251275738). RESULTS: Twenty-four randomized controlled trials involving 1, 792 unique participants (912 intervention and 880 control) were included. Exercise was associated with lower EPDS scores than usual care/non-exercise control (MD = -2.73, 95% confidence interval (CI) -3.57 to -1.88; I2 = 95%), representing an average effect across highly heterogeneous studies. Delivery format showed no difference in an omnibus comparison across three reported categories (p = 0.29), and intervention composition also showed no subgroup difference (p = 0.66). Interventions lasting <12 weeks showed a larger pooled effect than those lasting ≥12 weeks (subgroup p = 0.009), but this was exploratory. In the exercise-type network, yoga/mind-body exercise ranked highest (surface under th
articles.summary:
BACKGROUND: This systematic review and network meta-analysis examined randomized controlled trials (RCTs) of exercise-based interventions for postpartum depressive symptoms, comparing exercise modalities and weekly volumes using the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS). The study synthesized evidence to determine whether exercise reduces depressive symptoms and if specific types or doses are more effective.

FINDINGS: Twenty-four RCTs with 1,792 participants (912 intervention, 880 control) were included. Exercise significantly reduced EPDS scores compared to usual care/non-exercise controls (MD = -2.73, 95% CI -3.57 to -1.88; I² = 95%). Yoga/mind-body exercise ranked highest in the exercise-type network (SUCRA = 94.2%), with a modest estimated advantage over aerobic exercise (MD = -2.62, 95% CI -5.16 to -0.08). The 45–90 min/week volume category ranked highest (SUCRA = 84.6%), but no between-volume contrasts were statistically significant. Subgroup analysis suggested shorter interventions (<12 weeks) had larger effects than longer ones (≥12 weeks), but this was exploratory.

INTERPRETATION: The evidence suggests exercise may modestly reduce postpartum depressive symptoms, but high heterogeneity, indirect comparisons, and very low network certainty limit confidence in identifying an optimal exercise type or dose. The star-shaped network and mixed samples (prevention vs. treatment) further constrain conclusions. While exercise may serve as a useful adjunct, it should not replace clinical assessment or indicated treatments like psychotherapy or pharmacotherapy.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Exercise can be considered a low-risk adjunct in postpartum mental health care, particularly for mild symptoms, but clinicians should individualize recommendations and monitor response. The lack of clear dose-response or modality superiority means treatment choices should prioritize patient preference and feasibility over theoretical advantages.

articles.title: Ketamine and Esketamine in Acute Suicidal Presentations: Evidence, Limits, and a Conceptual Recovery-Enabling Downstaging Framework.
articles.authors: Słupska A, Cubała WJ, Świeczkowski D, et al.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To synthesize evidence for intravenous racemic ketamine and regulated intranasal esketamine in adults with acute suicidal presentations; distinguish the outcomes these interventions have and have not been shown to change; and place any rapid response within a complete emergency suicide-care pathway. METHODS: A narrative review of PubMed/MEDLINE-indexed literature was updated through July 16, 2026. Searches and study selection were performed by Wiesław Jerzy Cubała and Anita Słupska. Priority was given to randomized trials, systematic reviews and meta-analyses, pivotal ASPIRE publications, current US and European product information, and studies of emergency-department safety planning, lethal-means counseling, and post-discharge care. No formal risk-of-bias assessment or pooled reanalysis was undertaken. RESULTS: Intravenous racemic ketamine has randomized and meta-analytic evidence for rapid, short-term reduction of suicidal ideation in selected adults, with important variation by population, comparator, measure, and follow-up. The evidence does not establish prevention of suicide attempts or deaths. In ASPIRE I and II, regulated intranasal esketamine added to hospitalization, a newly initiated or optimized oral antidepressant, and comprehensive standard care accelerated improvement in depressive symptoms; clinician-rated suicidality improved markedly in both groups and did not consistently separate from placebo plus standard care. Across both evidence streams, a p
articles.summary:
BACKGROUND: This narrative review synthesizes evidence on intravenous racemic ketamine and intranasal esketamine for acute suicidal presentations in adults, aiming to clarify which outcomes these interventions affect and how they fit into emergency suicide care pathways. It prioritizes randomized trials, meta-analyses, and regulatory documents but does not perform formal risk-of-bias assessment or pooled analysis.

FINDINGS: Intravenous ketamine shows randomized and meta-analytic evidence for short-term reduction in suicidal ideation in selected adults, though effects vary by population, comparator, and follow-up duration. Intranasal esketamine (ASPIRE trials) accelerated improvement in depressive symptoms in hospitalized patients with major depressive disorder and acute suicidal ideation, but did not consistently outperform placebo in reducing suicidality. Neither intervention has evidence for preventing suicide attempts or deaths.

INTERPRETATION: The evidence base is limited by the lack of formal risk-of-bias assessment and absence of pooled reanalysis, reducing confidence in effect estimates. The short-term nature of observed benefits and lack of impact on hard outcomes (attempts/deaths) constrain clinical utility. The proposed "downstaging framework" is conceptual and unvalidated, offering a theoretical approach rather than evidence-based guidance.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Ketamine/esketamine may offer short-term symptomatic relief in carefully selected patients but should not be viewed as suicide-preventive. They must be integrated into comprehensive emergency care, including safety planning and risk formulation, without replacing standard interventions.

articles.title: Artificial intelligence EEG biomarkers for schizophrenia diagnosis: Systematic review with PROBAST+AI assessment.
articles.authors: Łoś K, Waszkiewicz N
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The application of artificial intelligence (AI) to resting-state electroencephalography (EEG) data represents a burgeoning frontier in schizophrenia diagnostics. However, the inferential validity of findings is frequently compromised by methodological heterogeneity. This systematic review rigorously evaluates the diagnostic efficacy and methodological robustness of AI-generated EEG biomarkers by implementing the Prediction model Risk Of Bias Assessment Tool for Artificial Intelligence (PROBAST+AI). METHODS: Following PRISMA guidelines, a systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science identified 43 primary studies encompassing 3,420 patients with schizophrenia or first-episode psychosis and 3,164 healthy controls (total N = 6,584). Methodological quality and validation strategies were assessed using the 34 signaling questions of the PROBAST+AI framework. RESULTS: The aggregate mean diagnostic accuracy across the literature was 93.38%, with deep learning architectures demonstrating superior metrics relative to classical machine learning (96.83% vs. 87.68%). Critically, external validation was restricted to 4.7% of the included studies. A pronounced performance discrepancy was observed between subject-wise (88.22%) and segment-wise (98.14%) validation protocols, indicating pervasive data leakage. Overall, 76.7% of the analyzed studies were characterized by a high risk of bias, predominantly stemming from suboptimal data partitioning and inadequate independen
articles.summary:
BACKGROUND: The review asks whether artificial-intelligence-enhanced resting-state EEG can reliably diagnose schizophrenia, synthesizing 43 studies (N = 6 584) under PRISMA guidance and rating risk of bias with PROBAST+AI.

FINDINGS: Pooled diagnostic accuracy was 93.38 % (deep learning 96.83 % vs classical ML 87.68 %). Only 4.7 % of studies used external validation; subject-wise validation yielded 88.22 % accuracy versus 98.14 % with segment-wise protocols, indicating data leakage. High risk of bias was present in 76.7 % of studies, mainly due to flawed data partitioning and lack of independent verification.

INTERPRETATION: The evidence base is methodologically weak: accuracies are likely inflated by data leakage and inadequate validation. The PROBAST+AI assessment shows high risk of bias in most studies, so the reported effect sizes cannot be trusted for clinical decision-making. Standardized, transparent validation is urgently needed before any bedside application.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Current AI-EEG biomarkers for schizophrenia diagnosis should not be adopted in routine care; centers should await externally validated, low-bias models before considering implementation.

articles.title: Clinical outcomes following five-day accelerated intermittent theta burst stimulation for treatment-resistant depression in routine clinical practice: A prospective naturalistic cohort study.
articles.authors: Khanna A, Espiritu A, Zhu L, et al.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Treatment-resistant depression (TRD) is a debilitating condition occurring in major depressive disorder (MDD) and bipolar II disorder (BP-II). Intermittent theta burst stimulation (iTBS) is an established neuromodulation approach for TRD, but standard delivery requires once-daily sessions over several weeks. Accelerated iTBS (aiTBS) may reduce treatment burden by temporally compressing delivery. We evaluated the implementation, tolerability, and clinical outcomes associated with a 5-day aiTBS schedule for adults experiencing TRD in MDD and BP-II. METHODS: In this single-center, open-label, uncontrolled, prospective naturalistic cohort study, adults with MDD or BP-II experiencing TRD received 30 iTBS sessions (600 pulses/session; total 18 000 pulses) over 5 days with 50-minute inter-session intervals. HAMD-17 was assessed at baseline, post-treatment, and 2-month follow-up. Secondary outcomes included Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9), Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7), baseline Clinical Global Impression-Severity (CGI-S), post-treatment/follow-up CGI-I, response/remission rates, and adverse events. Longitudinal changes were evaluated using linear mixed-effects models. RESULTS: Forty-six participants contributed longitudinal data (mean age 44.3 years; 54.4% male). HAMD-17 response rates were 28.3% (n = 13) post-treatment and 37.0% (n = 17) at follow-up; remission rates were 26.1% (n = 12) and 32.6% (n = 15), respectively. Improvements were also observed on
articles.summary:
BACKGROUND: This single-centre, open-label, uncontrolled prospective naturalistic cohort study examined whether a 5-day accelerated intermittent theta-burst stimulation (aiTBS) protocol (30 sessions, 18 000 pulses) is feasible, tolerable and clinically effective for adults with treatment-resistant depression (TRD) in major depressive disorder (MDD) or bipolar II disorder (BP-II).

FINDINGS: Forty-six adults (mean age 44.3 y, 54.4 % male) received 5-day aiTBS. HAMD-17 response rates were 28.3 % immediately post-treatment and 37.0 % at 2-month follow-up; remission rates were 26.1 % and 32.6 %, respectively. PHQ-9 and GAD-7 scores also improved. CGI-I showed 52.2 % improved post-treatment and 60.9 % at follow-up. Adverse events were mainly transient stimulation-site pain.

INTERPRETATION: The study demonstrates feasibility and tolerability of 5-day aiTBS in routine practice, with moderate short-term symptom reductions. However, the single-arm, unblinded design and lack of sham control preclude ruling out placebo effects or expectancy bias. The sample is modest, limiting precision of effect estimates. Randomised sham-controlled trials are required to confirm efficacy and durability.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: At present, 5-day aiTBS may be considered an experimental option for TRD when standard iTBS is impractical, but patients should be counselled that evidence for efficacy is preliminary and equipoise remains.

articles.title: Feasibility, Acceptability, and Preliminary Outcomes of a Group-Based Brief Cognitive-Behavioral Therapy Protocol for Suicide Prevention in a Brazilian Public Mental Health Service: A Mixed-Methods Pilot Study.
articles.authors: de Figueiredo LL, Beiram L, Santos JM, et al.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: We evaluated the feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary outcomes of group-adapted brief cognitive-behavioral therapy for suicide prevention (BCBT) in a Brazilian public psychiatric outpatient service. METHODS: This single-arm, nonrandomized, mixed-methods pilot enrolled 27 adults across two cohorts receiving 16 weekly group sessions. Feasibility and acceptability were assessed, and suicidal ideation was monitored weekly using the Beck Scale for Suicide Ideation (BSI). RESULTS: Enrollment targets were met; 70.4% had ≥ 4 recorded sessions, and no intervention-related adverse events were recorded. All six questionnaire respondents rated recommendation at 8-10. Four provided qualitative responses, highlighting shared suffering recognition and an interpretive theme of hope instillation. The linear BSI slope was nonsignificant (B = -0.29, p = 0.129); multiple imputation yielded B = -0.36 (p = 0.018). An exploratory quadratic model indicated greater decline later in treatment (p = 0.008). Among 18 participants with ≥ 4 recorded sessions and baseline BSI, scores decreased by 8.2 points from baseline to the last observation (d = -0.67; p = 0.011). CONCLUSIONS: Group-adapted BCBT showed preliminary feasibility and acceptability, with uncontrolled signals of reduced suicidal ideation. Controlled evaluation is needed to establish efficacy.
articles.summary:
BACKGROUND: This single-arm, nonrandomized mixed-methods pilot study in a Brazilian public psychiatric outpatient service evaluated the feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary outcomes of a group-adapted brief cognitive-behavioral therapy protocol (BCBT) for suicide prevention in 27 adults across two cohorts.

FINDINGS: Enrollment targets were met, with 70.4% attending ≥4 sessions and no intervention-related adverse events reported. All six questionnaire respondents rated the intervention 8–10 for recommendation, and qualitative feedback highlighted shared suffering recognition and instillation of hope. Weekly suicidal ideation (BSI) showed a nonsignificant linear slope (B = −0.29, p = 0.129), but multiple imputation yielded B = −0.36 (p = 0.018). An exploratory quadratic model suggested greater decline later in treatment (p = 0.008). Among 18 participants with ≥4 sessions and baseline BSI, scores decreased by 8.2 points (d = −0.67; p = 0.011).

INTERPRETATION: The study demonstrates preliminary feasibility and acceptability of group-adapted BCBT in a resource-limited public setting, with no safety concerns. However, the uncontrolled design precludes causal inference; the small sample and reliance on multiple imputation for significance weaken internal validity. The observed effect size (d = −0.67) is moderate but derived from a subset, and the clinical significance of an 8.2-point BSI reduction is uncertain without a comparator or longer follow-up. Further randomized controlled trials are needed to confirm efficacy and durability.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: This pilot suggests group BCBT may be feasible in public psychiatric services, but routine adoption is premature. Clinicians should await controlled trials before considering implementation, while monitoring for potential benefits in patient-reported hope and shared experience.

articles.title: Keeping the body in mind: Development of the Transdiagnostic Global Impression-Somatic Symptoms and Signs (TGI-3S) scale.
articles.authors: McIntyre RS, Barabassy A, Dombi ZB, et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: It is well-established that mental illness is associated with excess and premature mortality. Consequently, the assessment of physical health should be routine in the evaluation of persons living with mental disorders. Herein, we introduce the development of a global instrument to assess physical health status in persons with mental disorders. METHODS: Following the development of the Transdiagnostic Global Impression-Psychopathology (TGI-P) scale, a novel scale of physical health status, the Transdiagnostic Global Impression-Somatic Symptoms and Signs (TGI-3S), was created using similar principles. Scale development followed a multistage process involving (1) item generation using deductive methods, (2) two content validations by an expert panel, and (3) two iterative usability-testing rounds with patients and caregivers. These rounds therefore assessed understandability and ease of use for wording, visual format, and emotional/cognitive load of the instrument. The psychometric validation is underway. RESULTS: The TGI-3S was developed as a front-end screening tool resulting in a broad somatic burden map, rather than a diagnostic instrument. Throughout the development process, experts, patients, and caregivers evaluated the TGI-3S positively. In the final usability round, 96% found the aim of the scale clear, and 87% considered the instructions easy to follow. The scale demonstrated high-level usability, with 72% completing the TGI-3S in <5 minutes. Emotional and
articles.summary:
BACKGROUND: Routine assessment of physical health in psychiatric patients is clinically important but lacks brief, validated tools. This study reports the development of the Transdiagnostic Global Impression-Somatic Symptoms and Signs (TGI-3S) scale, a brief front-end screening instrument for somatic burden in patients with any mental disorder.

FINDINGS: The TGI-3S was created through deductive item generation, two expert panel validations, and two iterative usability-testing rounds with patients and caregivers. In the final usability round (n not specified), 96% found the aim clear, 87% rated instructions as easy to follow, 72% completed the scale in under 5 minutes, and burden was rated low with good item comprehension.

INTERPRETATION: The study describes an early-stage scale development process with promising usability metrics, but no psychometric validation data are yet available. The small usability sample and lack of reported reliability, validity, or inter-rater metrics limit confidence in the instrument’s performance. The TGI-3S may eventually support routine somatic screening, but clinical adoption should await full validation.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: For now, the TGI-3S remains a candidate tool rather than a recommended instrument; clinicians should continue using established measures for somatic assessment in psychiatric care until psychometric data are published.

articles.title: Longitudinal peripheral DNA methylation remodeling following ketamine-assisted psychotherapy in major depressive disorder.
articles.authors: Nepton A, Faber SC, Kaminsky Z, et al.
articles.abstract: Ketamine produces rapid antidepressant effects, but the molecular processes associated with their persistence remain poorly defined in humans. We examined longitudinal DNA methylation changes in 10 adults with major depressive disorder undergoing ketamine-assisted psychotherapy using two pre-treatment assessments (T1, T2) and one post-treatment assessment (T3). Participants received three sessions of intranasal racemic ketamine within a structured psychotherapy protocol. Buccal DNA methylation was measured using the Illumina MethylationEPIC v2.0 BeadChip. Depressive symptoms improved markedly following treatment, with mean Beck Depression Inventory-II scores declining from the severe to the mild range (p < .001). Of 802,595 CpG loci evaluated, 20,770 met the nominal T3-versus-T2 screening criterion. Sequential filtering for methylation-change magnitude and movement relative to pre-treatment fluctuation identified 962 retained CpG loci, including 517 retained gene-annotated loci. A supplementary linear mixed-effects analysis modeled repeated measurements within participants across the 603 preselected gene-annotated magnitude-filtered loci; because these loci were selected using the same contrast and cohort, this analysis was not treated as independent confirmation. Exploratory enrichment analysis of this 603-locus set identified NOTCH1-related Reactome terms driven by NOTCH1, DLL1, and ADAM17. Within the retained signature, multiple core and adjacent Notch-related components f
articles.summary:
BACKGROUND: This longitudinal cohort study in 10 adults with major depressive disorder (MDD) examined whether peripheral DNA methylation changes accompany clinical improvement after three sessions of intranasal ketamine combined with structured psychotherapy, addressing the molecular underpinnings of ketamine’s sustained antidepressant effects.

FINDINGS: Mean Beck Depression Inventory-II scores fell from the severe to the mild range after treatment (p < .001). Of 802,595 CpG sites, 20,770 met a nominal post- vs pre-treatment methylation change threshold; after filtering for magnitude and stability, 962 CpGs remained, including 517 annotated genes. A linear mixed-effects model across 603 preselected loci highlighted NOTCH1-related Reactome pathways driven by NOTCH1, DLL1, and ADAM17, suggesting coordinated Notch signaling changes.

INTERPRETATION: The study provides preliminary evidence of a structured peripheral methylation signature linked to clinical improvement, but the sample is tiny, lacks a comparator arm, and methylation was measured in buccal cells rather than brain tissue. The exploratory enrichment analysis was not independently validated, so causality and brain relevance remain uncertain. The effect size of symptom change is large, yet the methylation findings are hypothesis-generating only.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: These results do not yet alter practice; they suggest potential epigenetic biomarkers for further study, but routine use of methylation testing to guide ketamine-assisted psychotherapy is not supported by this evidence.

articles.title: Stimulant Persistence in Adult ADHD: A Retrospective Analysis of a Large Clinical Cohort.
articles.authors: Wettstein R, Pirgon E, Kroesen J, et al.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Network meta-analyses suggest dexamphetamines (dAMP) may yield more favourable short-term outcomes than methylphenidate (MPH) in adults with ADHD, yet evidence on long-term comparative persistence remains scarce. This study compared 12-month treatment persistence between MPH and dAMP in a large multicentre cohort and explored associations with ADHD clinical presentations and objectively measured core symptoms. METHODS: Stimulant persistence was defined by the primary outcome, 'time-to-transition', the interval from initiation to switching stimulant classes, transitioning to non-stimulants or complete discontinuation. Patients were censored at 12 months or at last clinical contact. A multivariable mixed-effects Cox proportional hazard model with a random intercept for clinicians was used to estimate hazard ratios (HR) and assess the relative impact of stimulant class on persistence, including its interactions with DSM-based clinical presentations and objective indices. RESULTS: Among 12,995 participants (49% female), 62% initiated dAMP and 38% MPH. Median time-to-transition was 33.1 weeks for dAMP versus 15.0 weeks for MPH. MPH was associated with a 45% increased hazard for non-persistence compared to dAMP (HR = 1.45, 95% CI [1.36-1.55]). Regarding clinical and objective factors, hyperactive/impulsive presentation (HR = 1.14, p = 0.025) and objective impulsivity (HR = 1.05, p = 0.002) were independently associated with non-persistence.
